psql.authority: A fixed conninfo meta-command on the exact persistent psql process used for the operation, correlated to transport invocation UUID and process lifetime.
requirements: Pinned image/tool and sanitized environment; internal exact hostname, port, database, username and CA path.
Explicit sslmode=verify-full; gssencmode=disable prevents a non-TLS encrypted substitute; no Unix socket/multiple hosts/hostaddr override.
Strict fixed-locale output parser obtains actual TLS protocol/cipher and current endpoint/db/user/port. Missing or non-TLS metadata fails before catalog or migration dispatch.
Successful connection under fixed verify-full establishes CA/hostname verification through libpq; conninfo alone does not independently prove certificate verification.
Reuse no metadata after process exit/reconnect or across invocations. No caller-supplied meta-command or SQL API.
psql.queryOrder: Risk/authorization -> client TLS proof -> DB identity/session guards -> backend observation -> ledger -> target function -> full catalog. Existing ledger/function early-stop contract retained.
psql.durableProof: Exclusive transport receipt persisted before yielding the session; UUID links plan/authorization/risk/package, client process and safe proof digest. Rechecks can reuse only a still-live same-process proof with unchanged configuration.

backupTools.authority: Actual successful pinned pg_dump/pg_dumpall database operation plus exact effective connection arguments, unchanged CA/credential-source identities and validated output. This is execution-bound enforcement evidence, not config-only evidence and not protocol/cipher telemetry.
backupTools.whySufficientDesign: For a TCP-only connection with explicit verify-full, trusted CA, fixed hostname and GSS encryption disabled, a successful real libpq database operation entails successful TLS/certificate/hostname verification. A config read, spawn event, return code from help/version, or another psql handshake is insufficient.
finiteInvocations: pg_dump FULL_CUSTOM with the exporter snapshot
pg_dump SCHEMA_CUSTOM with the same exporter snapshot
pg_dumpall ROLES_ONLY_NO_PASSWORDS with explicit initial database postgres
backupTools.implementationBoundary: Replace unchecked tool argument acceptance with exact internal profiles/validated fixed argument templates. Do not accept any caller-supplied conninfo/URI, endpoint, role, alternate database, jobs, help/version, output path or shell command. Snapshot ID remains the existing validated server-generated identifier.
effectiveParameters: host fixed TCP pooler hostname validated against pinned hash
sslrootcert /connection/root.crt with current authorization identity lock
processBinding: Fresh invocation UUID and tool/profile ID before spawn, pinned runtime, safe normalized parameter hash and CA identity.
Exact subprocess termination success; timeout/nonzero/missing process/output cannot produce valid proof.
Full/schema custom archive format and existing TOC/restore tests; roles-only complete output and existing no-password/restore checks.
Per-output SHA and invocation receipt SHA linked into backup manifest; a proof for another dump/process/run cannot substitute.
No additional diagnostic connection is opened to manufacture proof.

telemetry.reason: Not exposed by reviewed pg_dump/pg_dumpall interface; do not copy these fields from psql.

backupTools.backendObservation: unavailable for each dump client unless observed on that exact connection; retain exporter backend observation separately. Never label the exporter observation as the dump connection observation.
backupTools.trustBoundary: Relies on pinned libpq/tool enforcement and trusted local operator/kernel/image. These are existing operational trust boundaries, not proof of HOP B. Owned real-tool wrong-CA/hostname/non-TLS tests must pass before approval v4.

configurationIntegrity: Keep existing runtime credential/store identity checks. Pin endpoint/TLS parameters in an implementation-owned libpq parameter string supplied internally, without a password or logged full DSN. Recheck source identities before/after each tool. No writable non-operator service directory, uncontrolled env or library injection. No credential copy into evidence/temporary durable stores.
publicPrivacy: Never emit raw conninfo, stderr, argv containing a full connection string, passwords, DSNs, raw environment, certificate private material, raw dump or raw ledger/function bodies.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 17 SSL Support
sources.claim: verify-full requires certificate-chain and hostname verification.
sources.limit: Does not expose protocol/cipher observations for pg_dump.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 17 Connection Control
sources.claim: Explicit connection parameters take precedence over defaults; Unix sockets ignore sslmode; GSS encryption can supersede SSL unless disabled.
sources.designConsequence: Pin a single TCP hostname and port, explicit verify-full and gssencmode=disable; reject socket/multi-host/override paths.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 17 psql
sources.designConsequence: Parse a fixed command on the same persistent client process.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 17 pg_dump
sources.claim: Connection parameters may be supplied via dbname connection string; custom-format dump requires a real database connection.
sources.designConsequence: Only internal fixed connection parameters and exact dump profiles; no arbitrary dbname/options or help/version exits.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 17 pg_dumpall
sources.claim: Roles-only dumps global roles; explicit initial database avoids automatic postgres/template1 selection; no-password disables prompting.
sources.designConsequence: Restrict to roles-only, no-role-passwords, initial postgres, no-password, fixed connection parameters.

sources.title: PostgreSQL REL_17_6 pg_dump connection implementation
sources.claim: ConnectDatabase uses PQconnectdbParams and rejects unsuccessful connection status.
sources.limit: Public upstream source explains the mechanism; the actual approved image still requires owned tests and runtime image/hash checks.

sources.title: PostgreSQL REL_17_6 pg_dumpall connection implementation
sources.claim: Connection parameters reach PQconnectdbParams; connection errors do not establish a successful dump.
sources.limit: No per-tool protocol/cipher metadata is claimed from exit status alone.
